high: active water leak near electrical fittings
suspected structural movement or major structural crack
loose glass or window panel at risk of falling
low: minor hairline crack with no signs of movement

water_leak: Run the shower or basin in your own unit nearest the repaired spot for 10 minutes.
Look at the repaired area for new drips, damp patches or spreading stains.
Touch the repaired surface with a dry hand to check it is not damp.
Check again after the next heavy rain if the leak only appeared during rain.
plumbing: Open the repaired tap or valve fully and let the water run for 2 minutes.
Look under and around the repaired pipe or fitting for drips or pooling.
Wipe the joint dry with a tissue, wait 5 minutes and check the tissue stays dry.
Check the water pressure feels normal compared with other taps in the unit.
waterproofing: Pour or run water over the repaired area (shower floor, balcony) for 10 minutes.
Check the ceiling or wall below or next to the area for damp patches.
Look for water pooling instead of draining away.
drainage: Run the shower or tap that drains to the repaired trap for 3 minutes.
Check the water drains away without pooling.
Check for any foul smell near the floor trap.
sanitary_fittings: Flush the toilet or use the repaired fitting 3 times as normal.
Check the cistern stops filling after each flush.
Check the base or fitting does not rock and there is no water around it.
electrical: Switch the repaired circuit or appliance on and off 3 times as normal.
Use the repaired socket with a normal appliance for 10 minutes.
Check the breaker does not trip and there is no sparking, buzzing or burning smell.
Do not open the distribution board or touch any wiring.
If you see sparks or smell burning, stop, do not touch anything, and report it.
wall_crack: Look at the repaired area in good light; the crack line should not be visible.
Lightly run your hand over the surface; it should feel smooth and level.
Check again after a few days for hairline cracks returning.
structural_crack: Look at the repaired area from a safe distance; it should not show new cracks or gaps.
Check for flaking or spalling concrete around the repair.
Report immediately if you see the crack widening; do not lean on or load the area.
tiles: Gently knock on each repaired tile with your knuckle; a hollow, drum-like sound means it is not bonded.
Walk across the repaired tiles; they should not move, rock or click.
Look at the grout lines for gaps or cracks.
flooring: Walk across the repaired area; it should not creak, flex or lift.
Look for gaps, raised edges or uneven joints.
ceiling: Look at the repaired ceiling area from below in good light for sagging, cracks or open joints.
Check for damp patches or stains if the defect involved water.
roof: After the next rain, check the ceiling below the repaired area for damp or stains.
Do not go onto the roof yourself.
door_window: Open and close the repaired door or window 5 times; it should move smoothly without sticking.
Lock and unlock it; the lock should engage fully.
Check the gaps around the frame look even and no light or draught comes through.
paint: Look at the repainted area in daylight for bubbles, peeling or colour differences.
Lightly touch the surface once dry; it should not be tacky or flaking.
cabinetry: Open and close each repaired door or drawer 5 times.
Check hinges and soft-close parts work and doors line up evenly.
external_works: Look at the repaired area for cracks, gaps or loose parts.
After rain, check for pooling water around the repaired area.
other: Use the repaired item as you normally would.
Check that the problem you originally reported no longer happens.
